Skin Lesion Screening Study (Baseline Condition)

Welcome! In this study, you will evaluate 10 smartphone photos of skin lesions (plus 1 quick attention check) to determine if they appear Malignant (potentially cancerous) or Benign (non-cancerous).

  • Malignant: The lesion shows suspicious features (e.g., asymmetry, irregular borders, multiple colors, crusting/ulceration).
  • Benign: The lesion appears uniform, symmetrical, and non-cancerous.
  • Defer: The photo is out of focus, blurry, or not specific enough to determine if it is malignant or not.

You are not expected to be a medical expert—use the Example Lesions (left panel) and General Lesion Guidance (right panel) shown on screen at all times.

Examples of Lesions (Click any image to enlarge)

Melanoma (Malignant)

Asymmetrical shape, uneven dark brown/black colors, irregular border.

Basal Cell Carcinoma (Malignant)

Pearly/pinkish nodule, crusted or ulcerated center, visible vessels.

Actinic Keratosis (Malignant)

Rough, scaly, reddish-pink patch or dry crusted surface lesion.

Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Malignant)

Thickened red/pink scaly plaque, raised firm border, or crusted growth.

Normal Mole / Nevus (Benign)

Symmetrical, smooth border, uniform single tan/brown color.

Seborrheic Keratosis (Benign)

Benign "stuck-on" or wart-like tan/brown growth with clear edges.

General Lesion Guidance

ABCDE Warning Signs (Malignant)

  • A — Asymmetry: One half of the lesion does not match the other half in shape or appearance.
  • B — Border: Edges are irregular, ragged, notched, or blurred into surrounding skin.
  • C — Color: Non-uniform color; multiple shades of brown, black, pink, red, or white/blue patches.
  • D — Diameter & Form: Larger size (often >6mm) or raised, nodular, ulcerated, or bleeding surface.
  • E — Evolving / Texture: Scaly, crusty, oozing, or pearly/translucent surface appearance.

Signs of a Benign Lesion

  • Symmetrical shape: Round or oval with matching halves.
  • Uniform color: Even single shade of tan or brown.
  • Clear border: Smooth, well-defined edge.

When to Choose "Defer"

  • The photo is out of focus, blurry, or not specific enough to determine if it is malignant or not.
